headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage from shared PDF/document workflows; no prompt-injection or capability-conflict pathway is evident from the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway is not evidenced: agent_a has no clipboard, filesystem read/write, browser, or MCP surfaces, and agent_b only exposes PDF-file/browser-based test handling. With no shared communication channel or default ingestion path between them, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_a gains file-reading or browser ingestion, attacker-controlled PDF content could become instruction-like input.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not add clipboard-based handoff.
Disable any future shared MCP bridge unless provenance is tracked.
Review any new file-ingestion path before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches PDF documents and files, while agent_a is a document-processing system with no filesystem access documented. The pair can plausibly move document content through the workflow, creating a default-path leakage risk for sensitive PDFs even though direct exfiltration is not shown. Uncertainty about the handoff escalates this above low.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs are processed through both agents in the same workflow, document content may be exposed across the pair.
IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Use separate input folders per agent.
Strip sensitive pages before passing PDFs onward.
Process only redacted copies.
Log document transfers for review.
requires-engineering: add per-document access controls and provenance tracking.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write or mutable-resource capability is documented. agent_a cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP; agent_b supports multiple instances but exposes no write, git, or OAuth scopes. Without a shared writable surface, capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk should be reassessed.
IF shared mutable OAuth scopes are introduced, overlapping writes may occur.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable repo.
Run them in separate containers.
Add locking before enabling any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can consume PDF files and browser-based tests, so if it treats agent_a's document-processing output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream rendering or test actions. agent_a has no documented verification or citation guarantees, so the handoff is inferential rather than checked. The pathway exists in a default document pipeline, though not proven dangerous beyond work-product corruption.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as input without verification, cascading errors can propagate.
IF agent_b performs browser-based actions based on extracted text, incorrect facts may be operationalized.
mitigations: Insert a human review step.
Require schema validation on agent_a output.
Compare extracted facts against source PDFs.
Reject outputs lacking provenance.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_b handles PDF documents and agent_a is document-processing, so compliance concerns are limited to ordinary document handling rather than a specific regulatory breach. Because the profiles are sparse, this remains a low-confidence, low-severity compliance gap rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced, reassess residency and retention requirements.
IF one agent is deployed under stricter retention rules than the other, compliance mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Classify documents before processing.
Block regulated data until policies are confirmed.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Review vendor terms before deployment.
